title: Generic lissity of a constructible Weil sheaf over its finite-field model
statement: Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with the datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X_0$ be a reduced separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $(F,\theta)$ be a constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$ in the common-stage constructible-heart convention [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Thus $\theta:\Phi_X^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}F$, for geometric Galois Frobenius $\Phi_X$. There is a dense open subscheme $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ such that $j^*F$ on $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$ is lisse in the adic sense [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. The restricted Frobenius isomorphism makes this restriction a lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$. The empty scheme is included, with $U_0=X_0$.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1 and 4, generic lissity and finite-field-model choice; Deligne, Weil II (1.1.1), pp.146-147 supplies the constructible/lisse adic conventions.

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, take $U_0=X_0$. On the empty scheme the zero inverse system is a lisse integral sheaf and its rationalization represents the unique heart object, so the restricted underlying sheaf is lisse. Restricting the given isomorphism and its inverse gives the Weil structure. This includes $X_0=\varnothing$ and gives precisely $U_0=X_0$ in that case. Henceforth assume $X\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Paragraphs 1 and 4, including the empty-scheme convention of the item.

proof.text:
Base change makes $X$ separated of finite type over $k$ [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; $X$ and $X_0$ are Noetherian, being of finite type over fields [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. As $k_0$ is perfect and $X_0$ reduced, $X$ is reduced [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect]. The identity-induced equivalence $J_X$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] sends the heart of [def-weil-constructible-heart] used in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] into the heart of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]: $J_X(E,K)=(E,K)$ on integral representatives, and both standard pairs are cut out by the same ambient cohomology sheaves of an integral representative in the same integral category. By the final clause of that node, $F$ is lisse of finite rank [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] on the strata of a finite stratification $X=\coprod_

u$. $X$ has finitely many irreducible components $C_i$ [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] with generic points $\eta_i$ [lem-sc-scheme-sober]; the opens $V_i=X\setminus igcup_{j
e i}C_j$ are irreducible, pairwise disjoint, and $\eta_i\in V_i$. The stratum through $\eta_i$ meets $V_i$ in a locally closed set containing its generic point, hence in a set containing an open $W_i
i\eta_i$. Over $W_i$ the stratum immersion is a surjective immersion onto the reduced open $W_i$, hence an isomorphism, so $F|_{W_i}$ is lisse. Put $W=\coprod_iW_i$, an open containing every component generic point. Then $F|_W$ is lisse: extend the finitely many finite-stage lisse models to their compositum [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and take their disjoint union. Zero and unequal ranks are allowed.

proof.text: Let $p:X=X_0\times_{k_0}k\to X_0$ be the projection. It is integral: for any affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X_0$, its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{k_0}k)$, and $A\to A\otimes_{k_0}k$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change], since every element of the algebraic extension $k/k_0$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $k_0$. The integral-morphism criterion then implies that $p$ is universally closed. Put $C=X\setminus W$. Consequently $p(C)$ is closed, and $U_0=X_0\setminus p(C)$ is an open subscheme with $p^{-1}(U_0)\subset W$.

The open $U_0$ contains every generic point $\eta$ of $X_0$. Indeed, let $x\in X$ lie over $\eta$. By the finite irreducible-component covering of $X$ and sobriety, there is a component generic point $\xi$ generalizing $x$. Continuity gives that $p(\xi)$ generalizes $\eta$; maximality of the component with generic point $\eta$ and uniqueness of its generic point force $p(\xi)=\eta$. In an affine neighbourhood of $\eta$ and its affine inverse image, the points $\xi,x$ are comparable primes for an integral ring map, with equal contraction. Incomparability therefore gives $\xi=x$. Thus $x$ is a component generic point and belongs to $W$, by step 2. No point of $C$ can lie over $\eta$, so $\eta\notin p(C)$. Finally the finitely many components of $X_0$ cover it and are the closures of their generic points; since $U_0$ contains those points, its closure is all of $X_0$.

Write $U=p^{-1}(U_0)=U_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Its factorization through $W$ shows that $j^*F$ is lisse. Explicitly, restrict each finite-level locally constant sheaf of a lisse integral model on $W$ to the open $U$; it remains locally constant, and the tensor-transition isomorphisms restrict to the same isomorphisms. Rationalization and finite coefficient extension give the asserted lisse object at the common stage. The completed-system comparison identifies this restriction with the completed derived pullback on the constructible heart, which stays in that heart by [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres].

source.place: (1.1.1) b)-d), pp.146-147; completed pullback comparison as in Bhatt-Scholze Proposition 6.8.4.

proof.text: Because $U_0$ is an open of the finite-field model, the geometric Galois Frobenius preserves $U=p^{-1}(U_0)$ and $\Phi_X\circ j=j\circ\Phi_U$: on a base-changed affine chart both composites send $a\otimes b$ to $a\otimes\gamma(b)$. Pullback composition therefore gives an isomorphism $L\Phi_U^*Lj^*F\cong Lj^*L\Phi_X^*F$. Compose it with $Lj^*\theta$ to obtain $\theta_U:L\Phi_U^*(j^*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*F$. For the common-stage category this construction is made at a common finite coefficient field representing $F$, $\theta$, its inverse, and their inverse equations. The integral composition isomorphism of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] rationalizes at that field; passage to its common-stage class gives the displayed comparison. Its composite with the pulled-back inverse of $\theta$ supplies the inverse of $\theta_U$. By the fixed-pair definition this is a Weil sheaf, and step 5 makes it lisse. This completes every clause without asserting that geometric Frobenius is a $k$-morphism.
